newsitem.title: USA: US House panel probes Roussel Uclaf unit.
newsitem.headline: US House panel probes Roussel Uclaf unit.

text.p: A U.S. House Commerce subcommittee has asked the Food and Drug Administration to produce documents related to withdrawal of drug applications by Roussel Uclaf's Italian unit OPOS.

In a letter written to the FDA on Monday, Rep. Joe Barton, chairman of the subcommittee on oversight and investigations, said the panel had evidence regarding the applications "that may implicate FDA's fraud policy."

The FDA provided a briefing to the General Accounting Office on the situation but has so far failed to provide documentation requested by the GAO, the investigatory arm of Congress, Barton said in his letter.
The letter set a March 10 deadline for providing the documents.
Roussel Uclaf on November 8 said it had decided after meetings with the FDA to withdraw the Abbreviated Antibiotic Drug Applications for the drugs Cefaclor, Minocycline and Clindamycine Phosphate.
Roussel Uclaf is owned by German chemicals company Hoechst AG.
Reports at the time said the recall was prompted by the discovery that OPOS had failed to follow the manufacturing process required under the applications, said Barton, a Texas Republican.
In his letter, Barton also asked for copies of all documents related to a May 1996 FDA inspection of the manufacturing practices of Dutch biochemicals and food group Gist-brocades NV.
